observations.text: SP demonstrated airmanship at the level expected for this training unit, with the IP directing the order of the tasks and the timing of the operational checks throughout the sortie. Orientation inside the assigned area was maintained once the IP identified the reference points, and no significant rule of flight was violated. Marginal performance for the Training Section - self-initiated task sequencing and an independent cross-check of the Control and Performance Instruments against the A/C position are expected to develop in the following sorties.

SP maintained orientation inside the assigned area and performed the operational checks required by the Checklist and the SOPs, with the IP's verbal prompts needed only for the review of the fuel state during the working phase. No part of the sortie had to be directed or executed by the IP, and the decision to return to base was stated by SP after prompting, with the rationale given. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP put the tasks of the working phase in sequence without dropping any of them, and monitored the Control and Performance Instruments with reference to the outside visual cues during maneuvering. Two occasions of late attention to the fuel state were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention, and the hazard presented by the other traffic in the area was realized and positively avoided. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP kept accurate track of the A/C position, the fuel state and the remaining flight time throughout the sortie, and adjusted the execution of the profile to the time available in the assigned area. Contingencies and alternatives were identified, decisions were clearly stated together with their rationale, and all duties were carried out with minimum IP's supervision. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP correlated continuously what was happening in the A/C, in the assigned area and on the ground, and adjusted the execution of the mission to the remaining fuel and the prevailing weather without any prompting. Task loading was assessed before each phase, an alternative sequence was selected once in order to reduce it, and every decision was stated with its rationale. Knowledge of the rules and regulations regarding flight was complete and no task was dropped at any point of the sortie. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a task sequence that placed the area entry checks and the position cross-check at the same point of the profile, could not keep track of the A/C position relative to the assigned area boundary. The result was that the IP had to direct the recovery of orientation and execute part of the repositioning. Correlation of the A/C position with the area limits before the start of each maneuver is to be re-briefed.

SP, due to loss of situational awareness of the A/C position inside the assigned area, did not maintain orientation during the working phase and continued the profile toward the area boundary. The IP intervened, directed the turn back into the assigned airspace and took over the assessment of the fuel state for the remainder of the sortie. The sortie was not completed without assistance.

SP demonstrated airmanship at the level desired for this training unit, completing the operational checks and the review of the fuel state after the IP's verbal prompts. Orientation was recovered on each occasion, but recognition of the deviation from the planned profile was delayed until the prompt was given. Marginal performance for the Training Section - self-initiated correlation of the A/C position with the assigned area and with the remaining flight time is expected to improve.

SP kept track of the A/C position and of the fuel state during the working phase and adjusted the number of maneuvers to the flight time remaining in the assigned area. Two minor errors in the order of the tasks after the area entry were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP correlated the A/C state, the other traffic in the area and the remaining fuel throughout the sortie, prioritizing the tasks accurately and without dropping any of them. Actual and potential hazards were realized in time and the flight was regulated so that they were positively avoided, with decisions stated clearly and with their rationale. All duties were carried out with minimum IP's supervision. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP kept a complete picture of the A/C, the assigned area and the other traffic, and modified the sequence of the profile once the weather in the working area deteriorated, in order to protect the recovery fuel. Task loading was managed so that no phase of the sortie approached saturation, and the decision for an early return to base was taken on complete data and stated with its rationale. Knowledge of the applicable rules and regulations was demonstrated without any omission. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a working phase flown without any check of the remaining fuel against the recovery requirement, did not adjust the execution of the mission to the available flight time. The result was that the IP had to direct the termination of the maneuvers and execute the recovery decision. Management of fuel and time inside the assigned area is to be repeated under supervision.

SP, due to attention captured by a minor system indication while the aircraft state went unmonitored, dropped the clearing and the area orientation tasks for a prolonged part of the working phase. The IP intervened, took the A/C and re-established the position inside the assigned airspace. Task management that does not drive into a channelized attention situation is to be re-briefed before the next sortie.

SP, due to a task sequence that left the area entry checks to be completed inside the first maneuver, did not put the tasks in the required order and missed the initial assessment of the traffic in the area. The checks and the assessment were accomplished only after the IP's verbal prompts and the omission was recognized with delay. No rule was violated, but the working phase was not conducted with the independence required at this stage.

SP, due to lack of awareness of the fuel state during the working phase of the sortie, did not adjust the execution of the mission to the remaining fuel and continued the planned sequence of maneuvers. The recovery decision was taken only after the IP's verbal prompt, with recognition of the fuel condition delayed. The return to base was then flown safely, but the decision was not reached independently.

SP demonstrated airmanship within the desired standards, keeping track of the A/C position, of the assigned area limits and of the fuel state without IP's intervention. Task prioritization was correct, although on two occasions the clearing sequence was completed late because the position cross-check was given precedence. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency in handling the tasks of the working phase in sequence is expected to improve.

SP correlated what was happening in the A/C, in the assigned area and with the other traffic throughout the sortie, and prioritized the tasks accurately and rapidly during maneuvering. Contingencies and alternatives were identified before each phase, decisions were clearly stated with their rationale, and the profile was adjusted to the remaining fuel and flight time without prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP kept continuous awareness of the A/C state, of the area boundaries, of the other traffic and of the fuel, and modified the planned sequence of maneuvers when the working area became congested, in order to preserve safe separation. Task loading was recognized before it became limiting and an alternative course of action was selected to reduce it, with the reasoning stated to the IP. All duties were carried out without supervision and every step of each procedure was executed in the proper order. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a mission plan that contained no decision point for the forecast deterioration of the weather, did not identify the available alternatives and did not regulate the flight so as to avoid the developing hazard. The IP intervened, directed the exit from the working area and executed the decision to divert to the alternate airfield. The sortie could not be completed without assistance.

SP, due to mission-completion bias in pressing on past the briefed decision point, continued the working phase after the conditions for the recovery had already been met and did not gather all the available data before the final decision. The IP took the A/C and executed the return to base. Realization of actual and potential hazards, and regulation of the flight in order to positively avoid them, are to be repeated under supervision.

SP, due to a cross-check of the Control and Performance Instruments that was not re-established after each maneuver, did not keep track of the A/C position relative to the assigned area and of the remaining flight time. Orientation and the fuel review were restored only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the deviation recognized and corrected with delay. The remainder of the sortie was flown inside the area limits.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the transition into the working area, attempted the area entry checks, the traffic assessment and the setup for the first maneuver at the same time, and dropped the traffic assessment. The task was accomplished only after the IP's verbal prompt and the omission was recognized with delay. No loss of separation resulted, but no alternative course of action was selected to reduce the task loading.

SP, due to a fuel check interval longer than the working phase required, allowed the profile to run ahead of the planning for the flight time remaining in the assigned area. The shortfall was identified by SP in a timely manner and the last maneuver was replaced by an earlier recovery, without IP's intervention. The error was minor and the decision was clearly stated with its rationale.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic during the repositioning between two maneuvers, momentarily lost track of the A/C position relative to the assigned area boundary. The position was re-established by SP against the outside visual cues in a timely manner without IP's intervention, and the profile continued inside the area limits. Orientation, task prioritization and the assessment of the other traffic were otherwise maintained throughout the sortie.

SP demonstrated airmanship within the desired standards, maintaining orientation, correlating the A/C state with the assigned area and the other traffic, and carrying out all duties with minimum IP's supervision. Decisions were correct but were stated late on two occasions, and the rationale was provided only when the IP asked for it. Marginal performance for the Training Section - speed in reaching and clearly stating decisions is expected to improve while the present accuracy of the awareness picture is maintained.

SP correlated continuously what was happening in the A/C, in the assigned area and on the ground, and adjusted the execution of the mission to the remaining fuel, the available flight time and the prevailing weather without any prompting. Task loading was assessed before each phase, an alternative sequence was selected in order to keep capacity in reserve, and every decision was clearly stated with its rationale. Flight discipline was complete, with all published rules and regulations applied and every required step of each procedure carried out in the proper order. Above end of block MIF achieved.
